title: How a Wireless Charger Works in 60 Seconds 📱⚡ #shorts
description:
A wireless charger has a flat copper coil that makes a fast-changing magnetic field, flipping over 100,000 times a second. A matching coil inside the phone catches that field and turns it back into electric current, which is converted to steady power for the battery. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#wirelesscharging #technology #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A wireless charger never touches your phone's battery. It sends power through *thin air*.

steps.label: Coil
steps.text: Inside the pad is a flat spiral of *copper wire* called a coil.

steps.label: Magnetic field
steps.text: Alternating current flips the coil's *magnetic field* over *100,000 times* a second.

steps.label: Phone coil
steps.text: A second coil inside the phone feels that changing field, and it *induces a current*.

steps.label: Rectifier
steps.text: A chip turns that back-and-forth current into steady *DC* to charge the battery.

steps.label: Alignment
steps.text: The coils must line up and sit *a few millimeters* apart, or most energy is lost as *heat*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Coil, field, *current*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
